question: Point P is 8 km in the west of point Q. Point Q is 6 km to the south of point R. Point S is 10 km south of point Q. Point S is 12 km to the east of point T. Distance between points T and U is equal to the distance between points R and S and point U lies to the north of point T. What is the shortest distance between points R and T?
solution:
Drawing the figure according to the given information:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/194e2bb57d3eb8dfe4f85d38c4e7f31361efbf0fdbd06f3fa2078af7dd09ecdb.png] 

Shortest distance between points R and T = RT

Triangle RST is a right angle triangle and RS = RQ + QS = 6 km + 10 km = 16 km

**__CONCEPT:__**

Applying Pythagoras theorem-

**(Hypotenuse)² = (Base)² + (Perpendicular)²**

(RT)² = (TS)² + (RS)²

= 12² + 16²

So, RT = √400 = 20 km

Hence, the shortest distance between points R and T is **"20 km"**.
